nodes.community_name: Setup Command and Its System Seam (0)
nodes.rationale: Muddy's files are the core's (agents/muddy); setup only shapes them for Claude Code and a folder's AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Build and check the plugin helper
nodes.norm_label: build and check the plugin helper
nodes.rationale: The helper is built for each system in the core's folder and started once, checking its protocol and a version read from a version resource (on Linux the helper's own parser).

nodes.label: CI test job (unit and type tests)
nodes.norm_label: ci test job (unit and type tests)

nodes.label: Core ADR-0009: the core is its own package
nodes.norm_label: core adr-0009: the core is its own package

nodes.label: Core installed from a GitHub tag
nodes.norm_label: core installed from a github tag
nodes.rationale: The core lives in node_modules, built by its prepare script (allowed in allowScripts). A new core release is a new tag: npm install the tag, npm approve-scripts, drop the old allowScripts pin. An untagged core change is tried by linking the checkout beside this one; the tag goes back before a commit.

nodes.label: Core CONTEXT.md vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Use the core's words (mod, plugin, record, FormID, instance, project, patch) in code, docs and messages alike.

nodes.label: Definition of done (tsc, tests, docs, smoke)
nodes.norm_label: definition of done (tsc, tests, docs, smoke)
nodes.rationale: npx tsc --noEmit clean, npm test green, npm run build && npm run docs:tools leaving the reference unchanged, npm run smoke passing; CI runs all of it on Windows and Linux.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge graph (graphify-out/graph.json)
nodes.rationale: Built by the Python package graphifyy (uv tool install graphifyy); the npm package of that name is another project. Only graph.json and .graphify_labels.json are in git.

nodes.label: Guides served at runtime
nodes.rationale: The guides are part of the product, not side notes: served as MCP resources under <scheme>://guides/... and through readServerGuide; a guide of this server's own is added as an entry in PRODUCT.guides. The core's skills are served the same way.

nodes.label: Testing against a live MCP client (build, reconnect, MCP Inspector)
nodes.norm_label: testing against a live mcp client (build, reconnect, mcp inspector)
nodes.rationale: A registered client runs dist/index.js, so a change is visible only after npm run build and a client reconnect; npm run dev opens the MCP Inspector against the build.

nodes.label: Local-model eval rounds
nodes.rationale: Fixed modding tasks with an Ollama-served model, scored; the OpenClaw plugin's npm run eval from round 64. The tools are the core's, so what a round points at is fixed there, for this server too. Every round is in docs/research/local-model-evals.md.

nodes.label: What this server owns (the MCP side)
nodes.norm_label: what this server owns (the mcp side)
nodes.rationale: The tools are not here: everything they do is the core. This server owns only the MCP side (stdio and Streamable HTTP, routing from getTools(), connect/retry/latch, the gate and response budget in serializeResult(), healthcheck, resources, instructions), PRODUCT, npm run setup, its tool reference, its two guides and its research notes.

nodes.label: Plugin helper (the core's .NET helper)
nodes.rationale: Built in the core's folder by npm run build:helper; needs the .NET 10 SDK.

nodes.label: docs/research notes beside the repository
nodes.rationale: What was found out before deciding (engines, Nexus, Mod Organizer's file formats, the Spriggit spike, the local-model eval rounds); kept in the skyrim-modding-tools folder, not in this repository.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: operating system and mod manager are separate seams
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007: operating system and mod manager are separate seams

nodes.label: Windows and Linux CI matrix
nodes.rationale: Every push and pull request runs on Windows and Linux, per the core's ADR-0007; Markdown changes run too because the guides and skills are served at runtime and their tests read the real files.

nodes.label: Smoke test over real stdio
nodes.rationale: Fails on anything but JSON-RPC frames on stdout, which no unit test can see; with no game on a runner the server gets a non-existent SKYRIM_MO2_INSTANCE, starts, and healthcheck reports the instance unreadable.

nodes.label: Ask the graph before you search
nodes.norm_label: ask the graph before you search
nodes.rationale: Run graphify query / path / explain before a grep or source read, then read only the lines it pointed to.

nodes.label: Core-first changes
nodes.rationale: A change to a tool, an answer, a guide or a skill is made in the core, never only here: the core holds the tools and the OpenClaw plugin serves the same core, so both products stay in step. Read the core's AGENTS.md before changing one.

nodes.label: Never write to stdout
nodes.rationale: The server speaks MCP over stdio; anything on stdout that is not a protocol frame corrupts the stream and breaks every tool at once. Use the logger (stderr). dotenv 17 did it, so index.ts loads it quiet, and npm run smoke catches that kind.

nodes.label: npm install replaces the core's built helper
nodes.norm_label: npm install replaces the core's built helper
nodes.rationale: npm install replaces the core's folder and the helper built in it, so the helper must be built again after.

nodes.label: Tool reference is generated
nodes.rationale: docs/Tool-Reference.md is generated from getTools() and never edited by hand; after a change to any core getTools() run npm run build && npm run docs:tools; toolDocs.test.ts fails on a stale reference.

nodes.label: Update the graph after every change
nodes.norm_label: update the graph after every change
nodes.rationale: In a commit of its own right after the change: graphify update . for code (by syntax, no model); a changed document or image needs the semantic pass /graphify --update, since graphify update . refuses where a document's saved nodes would go missing.

nodes.label: Runs beside the game, no container image
nodes.norm_label: runs beside the game, no container image
nodes.rationale: The server reads the instance's files, the game's plugins and a Papyrus compiler from disk and runs the .NET plugin helper beside itself; a container reaches none of it without bind-mounting all at identical paths, and none can see a running mod manager.

nodes.label: server.json declares every variable read
nodes.rationale: Every variable the server reads, here and in the core's build, is declared in server.json; serverManifest.test.ts holds the two together.

nodes.label: Every tool declares annotations
nodes.rationale: The core's contract tests hold every tool to it, and server.test.ts checks the same on the wire.

nodes.label: Linux setup with Amethyst
nodes.rationale: Setup installs the .NET 10 SDK (with ICU, without which the helper does not start) through pacman, builds, offers the Papyrus compiler and registers the server; Amethyst and its profile are found by itself (Flatpak or ~/.config).

nodes.label: Manual client registration (Claude Code, VS Code, Claude Desktop)
nodes.norm_label: manual client registration (claude code, vs code, claude desktop)
nodes.rationale: Settings go into .env in the server's folder and a registration only says how to start the server (a client's env block would still win). Claude Code registers with --scope user, since a server registered for one folder is missing in all others. A JSON file is read by no shell, so ~ does not work in its args.

nodes.label: Mod Organizer 2 under Proton (experimental)
nodes.rationale: Built from the sources of MO2-LINT, Wine and Proton and tested against laid-out folders; never run on a real setup, and healthcheck says so in its notes.

nodes.label: Platform support (Windows + MO2 verified; Linux + Amethyst tested on its layout; Linux + MO2 under Proton experimental)
nodes.norm_label: platform support (windows + mo2 verified; linux + amethyst tested on its layout; linux + mo2 under proton experimental)
nodes.rationale: The server picks the operating system's side by itself and the mod manager from SKYRIM_MOD_MANAGER; the same tools and projects on each.

nodes.label: Let your agent set him up (paste-in prompt)
nodes.norm_label: let your agent set him up (paste-in prompt)

nodes.label: ChatGPT desktop app and Codex (~/.codex/config.toml)
nodes.rationale: ChatGPT in the browser reaches only servers on the internet; a public HTTPS address would open the mod manager to the web, so the desktop app is recommended.

nodes.label: Claude Desktop project with Muddy's instructions
nodes.norm_label: claude desktop project with muddy's instructions

nodes.label: mcpServers config for any MCP client (node dist/index.js)
nodes.norm_label: mcpservers config for any mcp client (node dist/index.js)

nodes.label: Muddy, the modding agent (a mudcrab from the shore below Riverwood)
nodes.norm_label: muddy, the modding agent (a mudcrab from the shore below riverwood)
nodes.rationale: He reads the modding skills before he writes a record, builds until the build says success, tells what he made and where, and leaves the mod manager alone unless asked.

nodes.label: Files npm run setup writes for Muddy (~/.claude/agents/muddy.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in the projects folder)
nodes.norm_label: files npm run setup writes for muddy (~/.claude/agents/muddy.md, agents.md and claude.md in the projects folder)
nodes.rationale: A file already there that differs from Muddy's (the user's own or an older Muddy) is replaced only after a yes.

nodes.label: Muddy's two files: SOUL.md and AGENTS.md (core agents/muddy)
nodes.norm_label: muddy's two files: soul.md and agents.md (core agents/muddy)
nodes.rationale: SOUL.md is who he is and AGENTS.md how he works; copying both into the folder an agent works in is the simplest setup, with SOUL.md pasted atop AGENTS.md for clients that read only AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Nexus requirements: Node.js 24 and git off-site, Mod Organizer 2 2.5.2 or later (Amethyst on Linux)
nodes.norm_label: nexus requirements: node.js 24 and git off-site, mod organizer 2 2.5.2 or later (amethyst on linux)
nodes.rationale: The .NET 10 SDK is not listed: the setup installs it.

nodes.label: Git LFS for project meshes and textures
nodes.norm_label: git lfs for project meshes and textures
nodes.rationale: Optional: the projects folder's .gitattributes sends meshes and textures to Git LFS once it is installed; without it git keeps them as ordinary files.

nodes.label: MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, VS Code, any MCP client)
nodes.norm_label: mcp clients (claude code, claude desktop, vs code, any mcp client)

nodes.label: Muddy, the modding agent (README section 'Modding with Muddy!')
nodes.norm_label: muddy, the modding agent (readme section 'modding with muddy!')
nodes.rationale: A mudcrab agent that reads the skills before he writes a record, builds until the build says success, and leaves the mod manager alone unless asked; set up per client, by npm run setup after a yes, by a paste-in prompt, or by copying AGENTS.md and SOUL.md.

nodes.label: npm run setup
nodes.rationale: One command installs the .NET 10 SDK if missing, builds the server and plugin helper, finds the mod manager, registers the server with Claude Code, Claude Desktop and VS Code, sets up Muddy and ends with a healthcheck; it asks before everything it installs, downloads, registers or writes. Updating is git pull && npm run setup.

nodes.label: OpenClaw plugin (skyrim-modding-tools-openclaw-plugin)
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw gets the same tools from the plugin instead of this server, set up with its own wizard, openclaw skyrim setup.

nodes.label: Eval record (docs/research/local-model-evals.md) and the OpenClaw plugin's npm run eval
nodes.norm_label: eval record (docs/research/local-model-evals.md) and the openclaw plugin's npm run eval

nodes.label: Change other people's mods only through patches
nodes.norm_label: change other people's mods only through patches
nodes.rationale: Other people's mods are changed only through patches, never in their plugins.

nodes.label: Care with a real backend (test instance)
nodes.norm_label: care with a real backend (test instance)
nodes.rationale: The server writes into a mod manager's instance (mod folders, the profile's mod and load order; with Amethyst its deploy rewrites the game's Data). Prefer read-only tools, work on a test instance (a Wabbajack-installed instance deletes every mod it did not install on its next update, and authors void support), ask before deploying into an instance you do not own.

nodes.label: Deploying with Amethyst open or closed
nodes.norm_label: deploying with amethyst open or closed
nodes.rationale: With Amethyst closed the server runs Amethyst's own CLI deploy; with it open the answer asks for Refresh then Deploy, because deploying behind its window would race it. A redeploy writes files in place, so hard links show the new plugin at once.

nodes.label: Close Mod Organizer before deploying (Proton)
nodes.rationale: Mod Organizer holds the profile in memory and writes it back on exit; on Windows the server tells it to re-read, under Proton it cannot yet, so deployProject refuses while this instance's Mod Organizer runs.

nodes.label: Filesystem MCP server beside this one (for clients without file tools)
nodes.norm_label: filesystem mcp server beside this one (for clients without file tools)
nodes.rationale: Records are edited with the client's file tools; a client that only connects Ollama to MCP servers (ollmcp, oterm) needs @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem allowed into the projects folder.

nodes.label: Local models through Ollama
nodes.rationale: Below 24 GiB VRAM Ollama defaults to a 4k context, too small for any agent: set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH. The model must make real tool calls (gemma4:26b and e4b do; code-completion models write calls as text). Measure a model with the plugin's eval before relying on it. Speed notes: gemma4:26b spills experts to system memory on a 16 GB card; Ollama 0.40.6 ran ~2.5x slower than 0.40.4.

nodes.label: OpenClaw served by the plugin, not this server
nodes.norm_label: openclaw served by the plugin, not this server
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw reads none of a server's instructions, prefixes its tools and hides them behind Tool Search for a local model; the OpenClaw plugin serves the same tools under their own names with the instructions and skills. An older registration lists every tool twice: openclaw config unset mcp.servers.skyrim.

nodes.label: Path settings read like a POSIX shell
nodes.norm_label: path settings read like a posix shell
nodes.rationale: Neither .env nor a client's env block passes through a shell, so every path setting is expanded as a POSIX shell would (~, $VAR, ${VAR:-default}, relative to the server's folder), on Windows too; %USERPROFILE%, $(...) commands and, on Linux, Windows paths are refused with the way to write them.

nodes.label: russo-2025 papyrus-compiler (Linux)
nodes.rationale: The Creation Kit's compiler is a Windows program; setup downloads russo-2025's into the server's tools folder, searched after PATH and before ~/tools. In rare cases its output differs byte for byte, not in behaviour.

nodes.label: First run in a throwaway profile or instance copy
nodes.norm_label: first run in a throwaway profile or instance copy
nodes.rationale: The first run on a setup someone plays goes into a throwaway profile (e.g. mcp-test) or a copy of the instance, with a throwaway project.

nodes.label: Wine prefix resolution (SKYRIM_WINE_PREFIX)
nodes.rationale: ModOrganizer.ini holds Windows paths (Z:\home\..., D:\...); the server follows each drive letter's link in the prefix's dosdevices, taking the prefix from SKYRIM_WINE_PREFIX or MO2-LINT's state.json; with neither only Z: is read. Jackify and Steam Tinker Launch need it named.

nodes.label: blender-mcp-no-stdin.py (starts Blender's MCP server with no stdin)
nodes.norm_label: blender-mcp-no-stdin.py (starts blender's mcp server with no stdin)
nodes.rationale: Started as blender-mcp.exe on Windows, the Blender it runs in the background waits on the client's pipe and every call times out after 120 seconds; the script gives that Blender no input and starts the server as uv installed it.

nodes.label: Work on a test instance
nodes.rationale: Deploys write into the instance's mods and profile, so a dedicated portable Mod Organizer on a clean game is the safe place to learn; a Wabbajack instance's update deletes every mod it did not install.

nodes.label: Muddy in Blender (arranging a cell by eye)
nodes.norm_label: muddy in blender (arranging a cell by eye)
nodes.rationale: Muddy exports a cell with exportCell and brings back what was moved, copied or deleted with importCell; with Blender's MCP server beside this one he arranges the cell himself, without a Blender window.

nodes.label: addPatch
nodes.rationale: An override changes the record itself everywhere; each copy starts from its current winning version so other mods' changes are kept.

nodes.label: buildProject
nodes.rationale: What has one right fix it writes into the file (corrected); what builds but likely not as meant is answered as built_with_warnings with the warnings first.

nodes.label: built_with_warnings status
nodes.rationale: The plugin is written and each warning says what to fix.

nodes.label: deployProject
nodes.rationale: Refuses when the project changed since its build, or when the deployed plugin was changed elsewhere (e.g. in the Creation Kit): pull that first.

nodes.label: editRecord
nodes.rationale: Changes fields by path with no old text to match, and can build in the same call (build: true).

nodes.label: editTerrain
nodes.rationale: Writes a project copy of each touched cell's landscape, keeping shared edges equal, and names the trees, rocks and buildings whose ground moved, since they float or sink now.

nodes.label: generateNavmesh
nodes.rationale: Builds the navmesh from the collision of floors, walls, stairs, furniture and ground, with no Creation Kit; run after placing, moving or removing objects, after editTerrain, or for a new room.

nodes.label: Light plugin
nodes.rationale: The game shows a light plugin's new worldspace without its ground, so newWorldspace makes a light project full.

nodes.label: Navmesh (the triangles NPCs and followers walk on)
nodes.norm_label: navmesh (the triangles npcs and followers walk on)

nodes.label: newWorldspace
nodes.rationale: Makes a light project a full plugin, because the game shows a light plugin's new worldspace without its ground; cell 0,0 holds a COC marker named <editorId>Start.

nodes.label: pullProject
nodes.rationale: Refuses while the project folder has uncommitted changes, so what the pull changes can be reviewed with git diff and undone.

nodes.label: Family: Records in the load order
nodes.norm_label: family: records in the load order

nodes.label: Blender (a cell arranged by hand or through Blender's MCP server)
nodes.norm_label: blender (a cell arranged by hand or through blender's mcp server)

nodes.label: Family: Blender, land and navmesh
nodes.rationale: Cells, ground and navmesh are made without the Creation Kit; some work still needs other tools: a new NPC's face needs the Creation Kit, distant land needs LOD from xLODGen.

nodes.label: Creation Kit work under Proton
nodes.rationale: Saved over Amethyst's link, the plugin is a file of its own in Data: deployProject refuses to overwrite it, pullProject reads it back, and the next deploy removes it so it no longer hides the mod's.

nodes.label: Vanilla script sources (Scripts.zip)
nodes.rationale: Unpack Scripts.zip into the game's Data with nothing deployed in Amethyst; unpacked while a profile is deployed, Amethyst counts the files as runtime output and moves them to its overwrite folder at the next restore.

nodes.label: Corrections buildProject writes itself (`corrected`)
nodes.rationale: What has one right fix (a FormKey copied into a new record, escapes copied out of a JSON answer, a field in the wrong place) is written into the file and listed.

nodes.label: Build warnings, each with the one call that fixes it
nodes.norm_label: build warnings, each with the one call that fixes it
nodes.rationale: The build warns of what would go wrong in game (an armor no one can wear, a missing mesh, an effect that does nothing, a chest under the floor), each warning naming its fixing call.

nodes.label: Mods made as text (one YAML file per record)
nodes.norm_label: mods made as text (one yaml file per record)
nodes.rationale: A mod is a project of YAML text, one file per record, that can be kept in git and is built into a real plugin and deployed into the mod manager.

nodes.label: HTTP settings (MCP_HTTP_PORT, MCP_HTTP_HOST, MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS, MCP_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT)
nodes.norm_label: http settings (mcp_http_port, mcp_http_host, mcp_http_allowed_origins, mcp_http_allowed_hosts, mcp_http_rate_limit)

nodes.label: SKYRIM_ACCEPTED_TOKENS allow-list
nodes.rationale: There is no remote API to ask: the backend is a Mod Organizer instance on this machine, so the token list is the whole authority, and nobody is accepted when it is unset. Every session shares one plugin helper and one load order.

nodes.label: Per-session bearer token
nodes.rationale: Each caller's token becomes its session's identity towards the backend: createBackend(env, { bearerToken }) builds one backend per session, so two people get two independent sessions, never one shared credential.

nodes.label: Host allow-list
nodes.rationale: Defence in depth for the rebinding case where the attacker's name resolved to this server; leave empty behind a proxy that rewrites Host.

nodes.label: Origin allow-list
nodes.rationale: DNS rebinding lets any web page post to 127.0.0.1, so binding to loopback is no access control and a proxy cannot help; the Origin header cannot be forged, so a disallowed Origin gets 403, requests without Origin (non-browser MCP clients) pass, and an allowed origin is echoed, never *.

nodes.label: Per-session rate limit (token bucket)
nodes.rationale: One agent in a loop looks like healthy traffic and can take a shared backend down for everyone; complements the proxy's per-address limit. Over it: 429 with Retry-After.

nodes.label: Session bound to its bearer token
nodes.norm_label: session bound to its bearer token
nodes.rationale: A session id is a routing key, not a credential (the MCP specification says not to authenticate by it), so every request must present the token that opened the session; only a digest of the token is kept.

nodes.label: stdio transport
nodes.rationale: The default: the client starts node dist/index.js, one process per client and user. The backend connects before the transport so a wrong credential or unreachable backend fails at startup with a diagnosis on stderr. stdout is the protocol channel, so the logger writes to stderr, dotenv loads quiet, and npm run smoke fails the build if anything else reaches stdout.

nodes.label: Streamable HTTP transport (MCP_TRANSPORT=http)
nodes.rationale: HTTP changes who connects, not what a session can do: one long-lived operator-started process serving many sessions at /mcp. Meant for a same-machine client preferring a long-lived server; bind to 127.0.0.1 unless it must be reached elsewhere, then put TLS in front.

nodes.label: TLS terminated in front of the server
nodes.norm_label: tls terminated in front of the server
nodes.rationale: Bearer tokens must not cross a network in clear text: a reverse proxy or ingress terminates TLS.

nodes.norm_label: third-party content, with permission (phostwood's crash rules, address library offsets, crash logger sse's log format)

nodes.label: healthcheck
nodes.rationale: Defined outside every handler and listed in every profile; reports the profile and what was withheld.

nodes.rationale: The tools, router, behaviour guide, skills and vocabulary live in the core, which this server and its OpenClaw plugin both serve; the core can also be used on its own.

nodes.label: Tool reference (generated)
nodes.rationale: Rendered from the tool definitions themselves (32 tools across 7 families), so it cannot drift from the code; never edited by hand.

nodes.norm_label: core docs/mcp-tools.md (rules, architecture, workflows, errors, troubleshooting)

nodes.norm_label: core skills/ (the modding knowledge served to agents)

nodes.label: Docs kept accurate: a doc/code contradiction is a bug
nodes.norm_label: docs kept accurate: a doc/code contradiction is a bug
nodes.rationale: The docs are kept accurate deliberately, so a contradiction between a doc and the code is fixed in one of them rather than worked around.

nodes.label: Withholding tools the backend does not support
nodes.norm_label: withholding tools the backend does not support
nodes.rationale: The server withholds any tool the connected backend does not support; tools/list is always the truth and healthcheck reports what was withheld.

nodes.label: MCP tool annotations (read-only, writes, destructive, idempotent, reaches outside)
nodes.norm_label: mcp tool annotations (read-only, writes, destructive, idempotent, reaches outside)
nodes.rationale: Annotations are hints for deciding what needs a human, not a permission system: nothing is enforced.

nodes.label: Answer ceiling enforced centrally
nodes.rationale: serializeResult() is the single funnel every answer passes through, so the core's responseBudget.ts covers a tool added tomorrow without being told.

nodes.label: Profile decides what is listed and routed
nodes.norm_label: profile decides what is listed and routed
nodes.rationale: A tool outside the profile is not callable, so the readonly profile genuinely cannot write.

nodes.label: Retry only what was refused before it ran, once
nodes.norm_label: retry only what was refused before it ran, once
nodes.rationale: isSessionExpired() answers true only for errors that prove nothing was applied; a credential the backend refused is latched and never retried, because retries lock a password account.

nodes.label: Core ToolError becomes McpError
nodes.rationale: The tools are the core's: nothing here builds a tool's envelope; serializeResult() passes the core's through and handleError() turns a ToolError into an McpError with the same code and message.

nodes.label: FOMOD installer
nodes.rationale: Takes two calls: the first installs nothing and answers the installer's steps with option ids, the second installs with choices.

nodes.label: LOOT (libloot, masterlist, the user's LOOT rules)
nodes.norm_label: loot (libloot, masterlist, the user's loot rules)
nodes.rationale: The first sort downloads LOOT's library and masterlist.

nodes.label: Mod order
nodes.rationale: The mod order decides loose files only; archives follow the load order of their plugins, and a loose file beats every archive.

nodes.label: sortPlugins
nodes.rationale: A preview first (moves named, nothing written); apply: true writes LOOT's order only when the user said so.

nodes.label: NEXUS_API_KEY (a premium account's, for downloads)
nodes.rationale: searchNexus and readNexusMod need no key; downloadNexusFile is offered only when Nexus confirms a premium account.

nodes.label: Nexus API acceptable-use policy
nodes.rationale: Personal API keys are tolerated for personal use; applications others use should register with Nexus (support@nexusmods.com: name, description, logo) for a single-sign-on slug. A page on Nexus makes this an application others use.

nodes.label: Merge patch (addPatch with merge)
nodes.rationale: A patch that names both plugins as masters keeps both plugins' changes, where a plugin move keeps only one's.

nodes.label: Only when the user said so
nodes.norm_label: only when the user said so
nodes.rationale: Tools that change the user's setup (mods enabled or disabled, load and mod order, ini settings) act only on the user's word.

nodes.rationale: AI-Generated Content covers the code written with Claude; AI Media covers the banner, tile and page text. A mod without the tags its content needs may be moderated (Nexus, 2026-07-31).

nodes.label: The file's options (mod manager download off, primary file, requirements popup on)
nodes.norm_label: the file's options (mod manager download off, primary file, requirements popup on)

nodes.label: Custom permissions, open as GPL-3.0 has it
nodes.norm_label: custom permissions, open as gpl-3.0 has it
nodes.rationale: Upload, modify, convert and reuse with credit, the same license and the source; Nexus's recommended settings forbid what GPL-3.0 allows.

nodes.label: Release zip packed by git archive
nodes.norm_label: release zip packed by git archive
nodes.rationale: The main file is the repository at a release tag packed by git, so it holds exactly what is committed; unpacked, npm run setup takes it from there as from a clone, and only git pull needs the clone. Nexus file names are at most 50 characters.

nodes.label: Nexus v3 API (updates the description, uploads file versions)
nodes.norm_label: nexus v3 api (updates the description, uploads file versions)
nodes.rationale: A new mod page can only be created on the website; afterwards Nexus's v3 API can update its description and upload new file versions.
